Mira Shah: Hey team — filing my first PR against `repo/inference-runtime`. a few quick Qs: what's our preferred branching pattern, commit message style, and any hard limits on PR size? also, who do I tag for a first-time contributor review?
Jamal Cole: welcome! :tada: Branching: feature branches off `main` with `feat/<short-desc>` or `fix/<short-desc>`. Small PRs are appreciated.
Mira Shah: thanks — any concrete size guidance? e.g., max LOC or files?
Ryan T.: we try to keep changes under ~300 LOC and < 10 files for fast review. bigger refactors should be split or have a design explainer in the PR body.
Mira Shah: good call. what about commits — squash on merge or keep history? any commit message format?
Jamal Cole: we squash on merge for feature/fix PRs. Use conventional-ish messages in the PR title like `feat: add prefix cache support` or `fix: handle EOF in kv-reader`. In the PR body include a short summary, why, and rollout/rollback notes if relevant.
Katy (devx-bot): Automated reminder: all PRs must pass CI (unit + integration) and run `pre-commit` checks. See https://redwood.dev/x/ci-policy for details.
Mira Shah: CI note — if a flaky test fails, what's the workflow? do we rerun, or mark flaky?
Ryan T.: rerun once, if still failing open an issue and mark with `flaky-test`. Don't merge until green unless it's a docs-only PR.
Mira Shah: who should I request as reviewers? I don't see CODEOWNERS for that path.
Jamal Cole: for runtime changes ping @ryan and @mira-owner (actually i'm jamal but tag ryan and the runtime team `@eng-runtime`). If it's infra adjacent add `@eng-infra`. For first PRs, add `@onboarding` and we'll triage to a reviewer.
Mira Shah: great — do we require an ADR or design doc for small performance tweaks?
Ryan T.: small perf tweaks usually ok with a short benchmark note in the PR. Anything that touches scheduler/allocators or changes latency numbers by >5% needs an ADR and perf CI.
Mira Shah: pre-commit hooks — how to run locally? formatting?
Jamal Cole: run `pre-commit run --all-files`. We enforce `gofmt`, `black` for py, `ruff`, and `eslint` for TS. There's a repo-level `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
Mira Shah: is there a checklist or PR template I can copy to avoid missing steps?
Katy (devx-bot): PR template: - Short description; - Motivation; - Tests added; - CI status; - Rollout plan; - Linked issues/PRs. Use the `Create new PR` flow which pre-fills the template.
Mira Shah: thanks — last question: do we use labels like `needs-review`, `good-first-pr`, or `release-blocker`?
Jamal Cole: yes — `needs-review`, `blocking-release`, `perf-regression`, `flaky-test`, `docs`. Use `good-first-pr` only if you added extra explanation for new contributors.
Mira Shah: perfect, I'll open the PR now and tag `@onboarding`. appreciate the quick answers :bow:
